structure: Part 3, address-book edit and delete. Read in full: edit.fit.spec.js (7 tests) and delete.fit.spec.js (4 tests) in trade-imports-ins-frontend, plus axe.js for the axe tags, and all 11 trace zips the part names. The tim trace CLI refused every zip (TraceVersionError: trace created by a newer Playwright than tim's viewer), so each trace was mined from its unzipped raw files in this part's work folder (edit-prefill 759a1, edit-axe dafdd, edit-rejected af334, edit-email e9676, edit-erraxe dd003, edit-save de4e5, edit-cancel 36446, del-confirm 967cd, del-cancel d5c0d, del-yes fe6bc, del-axe 7d4d4): the test.trace step list (every navigate, fill, click and expect with its locator), the 1-trace.network log (method, URL, status, Location, form body) and the rendered HTML resources. Action ids in refs are the test.trace callIds (pw:api@N, expect@N). Pages, in order: (1) Edit address details, /address-book/{id}/edit, always reached by direct navigation after stub sign-in; its validation error state (HTTP 400 re-render, same URL), driven by an empty name and by a malformed email; save (302 to /address-book with a success banner) and Cancel (302 to /address-book, nothing saved). (2) Delete address, /address-book/{id}/delete, a confirmation with a warning button and Cancel; Cancel 302s to the details page /address-book/{id}, confirming 302s to /address-book with a success banner and, for the only address, the empty state. The address book list and details pages appear only as landing pages; part 2 owns them. Every surface is entirely govuk-* inside main. Axe runs on the edit page, its error state and the delete page, each with no violations of any impact. Gaps recorded: other edit validation messages, unknown or foreign ids, downstream failure, the entry controls, editing country and optional fields, and the effect of deleting an address in use.

claims.statement: A signed-in user reaches the edit address page at /address-book/{id}/edit for an address in their organisation's address book.

claims.note: That they match the add form rests on the shared fieldLabels helper in address-form.js; the add page itself is another part's.

claims.statement: Every edit field is prefilled from the stored address: name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, country, phone and email carry the stored values, and the optional address line 2 and county are empty when nothing is stored.

claims.statement: Town or city is a text input named 'townOrCity', two-thirds width.

claims.statement: Postcode is a text input named 'postcode', labelled 'Postcode or Zip code', at the fixed width of 10 characters.

claims.note: Back goes to /address-book/{id}; Cancel goes to /address-book. Recorded, not reconciled.

claims.statement: Edit and delete are scoped to the signed-in user's organisation: each test signs in as its own organisation id through the stub sign-in, and the same address id 000000000000000000000001 resolves in every organisation's own store.
claims.ref: every part 3 trace action pw:api@29 Navigate /auth/stub-sign-in?organisationId=...; edit.fit.spec.js lines 114-116
claims.quote: Saving mutates the stub's per-organisation store, which is shared across parallel workers, so this test needs an organisation of its own.
claims.note: Inferred from the spec comments and per-test organisation ids; the browser never sees the store.

claims.statement: The address-book API calls behind edit and delete (reading the stored address, updating it, deleting it) happen server side and never appear in the browser's network log, so their shape is not shown.
claims.ref: network logs of traces de4e5 and fe6bc: only frontend routes /address-book/{id}/edit, /address-book/{id}/delete and /address-book

claims.statement: No trace opens edit or delete for an address id that does not exist or belongs to another organisation, so the not-found or forbidden behaviour is not shown.
claims.ref: edit.fit.spec.js, delete.fit.spec.js

claims.statement: No trace shows what happens when the save or delete fails downstream (the address-book service erroring or unavailable).
claims.ref: edit.fit.spec.js, delete.fit.spec.js

claims.statement: No trace reaches the edit or delete page by its Edit or Delete control on the address details page: every test navigates straight to the URL, so the entry points themselves are not shown in this slice.
